object.short_description: Stepped, roughly square pyramid with a small block-like structure on its summit, standing on an irregular undulating ground patch; single grey textured mesh with a noisy, scan-like surface.

estimated_real_size.basis: File units are unknown (largest extent 0.6524, metres or arbitrary); no scale reference visible.

structure.overall_shape: stepped square-based pyramid with a summit structure, embedded in a rectangular ground patch

components.name: stepped pyramid body
components.description: Tapering body with several receding terraces visible on the stepped side faces and as concentric outlines in the top view; the pyramid appears slightly rotated relative to the ground patch edges.

components.name: summit structure
components.description: Dark, irregular block-like mass on top, narrower than the top terrace; it may be a small temple or a shrine, or partly eroded or reconstructed masonry.

components.name: ground patch
components.description: Irregular, undulating surface with dense triangulation surrounding the pyramid and forming a rectangular tile, with curling edges.

components.name: side stair or ramp strip
components.description: Darker vertical strip or notch running up at least one face (front and back views), possibly a staircase or an erosion channel.

repeated_elements.what: terrace steps with a fine block-like relief pattern on the treads

defects: ground patch with warped, curling edges
dark, blobby summit geometry, possibly occlusion or reconstruction artefacts
single grey colour reading (texture is almost uniform grey)

evidence.statement: Side views show a tapering stepped body with several receding terraces and a smaller structure at the apex.
The top view shows concentric, roughly square terrace outlines around a small central block.
A rectangular ground patch with undulating, curling edges surrounds the pyramid, so terrain is included in the model.
The mesh is a single component and is not watertight (508 boundary edges), with irregular triangulation and a 4096x4096 texture. This is typical of a reconstructed surface.
Symmetry scores are low on all axes, and no periodic pattern is detected; the form is irregular rather than ideally regular.
The up-axis heuristic has low confidence (0.25), but the views show the pyramid standing upright with the summit pointing up in the analysis frame (up = y in file coordinates).
The colour is uniformly grey (saturation 0), so there are no colour cues about material or origin.
The summit structure is dark and irregular and the terrace edges are partly blocky and eroded-looking, which could indicate ruined or weathered masonry, or could be a reconstruction artefact.
No scale reference exists in the views or facts; the unit of the coordinates is unknown.
